newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 15.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--The government's economic team will be meeting this morning on additional measures to cut back public spending. New legislatiion is expected to be submitted to Parliament within the day.

--Interest rates on Monday's issue of two-year zero coupons are hovering at the 10.5 percent mark. The finance ministry believes the issue will draw great demand as 12-month titles to be issued next year will carry less interest.
--An Athens court rules that the finance ministry has no constitutional right to close down businesses found guilty of tax crimes.
--The Statistical Service's new consumer price index will slight increase the rate of de-escalation of inflation.
IMERISIA

--The government is going ahead with the partial privatisation of state-run organisations and bodies (DEKO), as well as the second share offer for OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation. Sources say that the government is thinking of issuing DEKO bonds within the year which will transform into shares in 5-7 years.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou alerts the Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) to the fact that the private sector is delaying in the absorption of EU funds, with the result being a danger of funds being cut back.
--An impressive rise in industrial investment in Greece is on the cards for 1997, the European Union says.
KERDOS
--The State General Accouting Office has drafted a memo for all ministries and state-run bodies, saying credits will not be extended if they are not managing their finances and spending properly.
--Banks' profits have been affected by the pressures of lower interest rates on state titles.
EXPRESS
--A new era in energy began yesterday with the inauguration of the natural gas network. Prime Minister Costas Simitis called it the "biggest energy project in Greece since electrification".
--The national economy and finance ministry will host a meeting today on fiscal developments and the implementation of the state budget.
--Tax declaration forms for fiscal year 1996 have begun to be sent to tax-payers.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The inter-ministerial committee is set to approve six privatisations, beginning with the Elefsina Shipyards, at its meeting today.
--Ergo bank announced net profits of 44 billion drachmas for 1996, an increase of 18 percent over the previous year. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
